function.mechanism: Hydrolyzes bacterial peptidoglycan (especially Gram-positive bacteria), helping control spoilage and malolactic-related instability.

adi.basis: No numeric ADI identified in EFSA lysozyme opinions reviewed; conclusions are qualitative (no safety concern under intended use except allergenicity in susceptible individuals).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no general safety concern under intended conditions of use, except possible adverse allergic reactions in susceptible (egg-allergic) individuals.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR Title 21 eCFR search returned no current lysozyme food-additive GRAS section; lysozyme use conditions are listed in 27 CFR 24.246 (FDA advisory opinion; wine use up to 500 mg/L).

concerns.summary: Residual lysozyme in treated wine/beer/cheese may trigger allergic reactions in susceptible egg-allergic individuals.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA opinions report no general safety concern under intended conditions of use aside from allergenicity in susceptible individuals.
JECFA assigned ADI as not specified for lysozyme hydrochloride (1992).

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI was set (JECFA: not specified; EFSA opinions reviewed did not set a numeric ADI). Risk characterization is driven mainly by allergenicity rather than ADI exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations indicate low general toxicological concern under intended uses, but there is a credible and established allergenic risk for susceptible egg-allergic consumers.
key_factors: EFSA no-general-safety-concern conclusions under intended conditions
Documented allergenicity caveat for sensitized individuals
Current U.S. CFR evidence supports controlled wine-use conditions (27 CFR 24.246)
